Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 3 - No above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until samples and/or photographs of all materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. - cladding details, window/glazing treatment (including sections/reveals), roof, entrance doors and external door frames and any other external materials/details to be used.
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order that the Council may be satisfied as to the details of the development in the interests of the visual amenity of the area

Condition : 4 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development Order) 1995 (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order), no enlargement of the premises or any additional structures/buildings/enclosures within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out, other than as shown in the approved drawings, and no additional floor space shall be formed within the building(s) hereby permitted by means of internal horizontal division (new mezzanine level) without prior written approval of the local planning authority.
Reason: To protect neighbours' living conditions, highway conditions, the character and appearance of the area and to prevent over-intensive use of the site.

Condition : 5 - The premises are restricted to the uses specified within this permission and shall not be used for any other purpose, including any use falling under Classes B2, B8, E(g)(ii) and E(g)(iii) of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), nor in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification. Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining properties but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Use Class to protect nearby land uses, highway conditions and the character of the area.

Condition : 6 - (a) The hereby approved development must be carried out in accordance with the approved Energy Statement.
(b) Prior to first occupation of any building within the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and to include As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions, and achieved a 100% reduction in emissions. This shall also include details regarding capped connections provided for the prospective district heat network.
(c)
Prior to first occupation of the hereby approved development, where a contribution is found necessary to achieve compliance with zero-carbon requirements of the Development Plan, the developer shall have entered into a binding agreement with the Local Planning Authority to pay any carbon offset contribution at the published rate in-force at the time of submitting details pursuant to Part B of this condition.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 7 - The development shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of delivery notes, invoices or installation contracts) have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development meets the following:
- At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.
- At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
- No construction or insulation materials are to be used which will release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.

Condition : 8 - (a) Within nine months of work starting on site, a BREEAM Design Stage certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) for Unit 1 must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority to show that an 'Outstanding' rating will be achieved in accordance with approved documents.
(b) Within nine months of the date of first occupation of Unit 1 hereby permitted, a BREEAM Post-Construction Review certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority to show that an 'Outstanding' rating has been achieved.
Reason: In order to ensure the highest standard of sustainable design and construction.
Supporting notes: Details submitted should state if BREEAM will be fully fitted, shell and core or shell only. Additional BREEAM Refurbishment and Fit-Out details will likely be required where not specified as fully fitted.

Condition : 12 - Prior to the occupation of each phase of the development, a post-construction monitoring report should be completed in line with the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance. The report should be submitted to and approved by the LPA in writing.
Reason: In order to maximise the re-use of materials and in the interests of sustainable waste management.
Note:
Once the Post-Construction Monitoring report is approved by the LPA, the Applicant should provide the approved post-construction monitoring report and any supporting information to the GLA at circulareconomystatements@london.gov.uk.

Condition : 13 - Prior to the occupation of each phase of the development, the post-construction tab of the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment template should be completed in line with the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment Guidance. Together with any supporting information, it should be submitted to, and approved by the LPA in writing.
Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to maximise on-site carbon dioxide savings
Note:
Once the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment is approved by the LPA, the Applicant should provide this Assessment together with any supporting information to the GLA at: ZeroCarbonPlanning@london.gov.uk.

Condition : 14 - .No fans, louvres, ducts, or other external plant shall be installed on the building(s) hereby permitted without the prior written approval of the local planning authority.
Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the area and neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 15 - (a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation, and air
conditioning (HVAC) to which this permission refers, shall be 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, at all times that the plant operates. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance to the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved.
(b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter.
(c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) to which the application refers, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again. This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the required standard. Once achieved, the plant shall be maintained permanently thereaf

Condition : 16 - 1. Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design, including drawings and supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form] to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the submitted Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy Report (29/04/2025) and associated drawings. The applicant must provide infiltration testing results to BRE365 to confirm whether infiltration is feasible at the site. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development.
2. Each of the units hereby permitted shall not be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for each unit has been completed in accordance with the submitted details for the site. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: To comply with the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems, the National Planning Policy Framework (Paragraph 103), the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13), along with associated guidance to these policies and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.

Condition : 17 - The development shall not be occupied until confirmation is provided that either:
(i) All necessary upgrades to the foul water network to accommodate additional flows from the development have been completed; or
(ii) A phasing plan for development and infrastructure, agreed with Thames Water and the Local Planning Authority, is in place. Where such a plan exists, no occupation shall occur other than in accordance with the approved phasing schedule. Reason: Network reinforcement is likely to be required to support the proposed development. These upgrades are essential to avoid the risk of sewer flooding and pollution incidents. Please note where network modelling is required, Thames Water will need confirmation of outline planning permission, a development phasing plan, and evidence of land ownership to be submitted to devcon.team@thameswater.co.uk . Modelling can take 9-12 months to complete and will not commence until these have been provided.

Condition : 19 - The development hereby approved shall provide no more 104 car parking spaces than in accordance with dwg no 11333_PL101B.
Reason: In order to control the level and usage of parking on the site and to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 21 - Before each phase of the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery & Servicing Plan (including details of the end occupiers of the industrial units, vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place, waste management) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 22 - Prior to the first use or occupation of the development full details (including manufacturers' specifications) of secure covered cycle parking facilities including large format cycles, that accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before the development is first occupied or brought into use. The approved facilities shall be thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 23 - The electric vehicle charging points as shown on the approved plan(s) and documents shall be installed and all active charging points made operational within 6 months of first occupation of each of the building(s) to which they relate and shall be permanently retained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Condition : 24 - No development shall take place until an Ecological Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
The Ecological Management Plan shall incorporate:
a) measures, including toolbox talks, to protect breeding birds, nests and eggs from mortality/damage, injury and disturbance, including avoidance by timing and/or appropriate supervision.
b) a watching brief for bats/and nesting birds and biosecurity measures with respect to invasive non-native species.
c) eradication and control (biosecurity measures) of invasive non-native species.
d) a scheme for the protection of the retained trees, in accordance with BS5837:2012. A plan to a scale and level of accuracy appropriate to the proposal that shows the position, crown spread and Root Protection Area of every tree on site in relation to the approved plans and particulars. The positions of all trees to be removed shall be indicated on this plan. A schedule of tree works for all the retained trees, specifying pruning and other remedial or preventative work, whether for physiological, hazard abatement, aesthetic, or operational reasons. All the tree work shall be carried out in accordance with BS3998:2010.
e) details of ecological enhancement, green walls and roof and urban greening factor, including how the urban greening factor is to be delivered and achieved on site;
f) an ecological lighting plan;
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area and to promote biodiversity.

Condition : 25 - Notwithstanding the details submitted, no development shall take place (including vegetation clearance, demolition, and ground works) until a Construction Environment Management Plan has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The Plan shall include:
a) Identification of stages of works, details of working hours
b) Risk assessment and mitigation measures for noise and vibration, dust and air pollutants, land contamination, ecology and ground water.
c) Setting up of site- protective fences, exclusion barriers and warning signs
d) Details of the ecological clerk of works or responsible person and lines of communication,
e) Watching brief for bats, birds, reptiles and amphibians including details of the pre-development checks, and, identified on maps where applicable, measures to mitigate the impacts of construction activities on wildlife, construction lighting plan, and details of any licensing requirement
f) Protocol for non-native invasive species, unexpected fauna if encountered on site
g) Communication with the neighbouring residents in order to safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area in general.
The approved CEMP should be followed and implemented throughout the construction period in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat and secure opportunities for the enhancement of the nature conservation value of the site.

Condition : 27 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include;
(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat,
(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development,
(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and
(f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years.
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 28 - Notwithstanding the submitted details, no above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until a habitat management plan in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for on-site and off-site enhancements must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The habitat management plan shall include:
(a) Prescription for management actions.
(b) Preparation of the work schedule (including an annual work Plan for over 30-year period and who will carry out the jobs mentioned in the management plans).
(c) Details of the body or organisation responsible for implementation of the plan.
(d) Time frame for reviewing the plan.
(e) Details of the management plans and its communication to the occupiers of the development.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 29 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
Following the completion of the Phase I desk study report, if intrusive investigations or gas monitoring is recommended, a Phase II site investigation must be undertaken.
No development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.
The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i) The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work.
(ii) The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii) Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the local planning authority may stipulate if this report is found to be insufficient or where it is deemed necessary to

Condition : 30 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i) The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii) The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority.
(iii) Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv) The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 31 - During the development:
The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues.
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i) Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(ii) In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii) The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 32 - Prior to the development is first brought into use:
The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i) The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement.
(ii) This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii) The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 33 - If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the local planning authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice.
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice.
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.

Condition : 34 - The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the approved documents (Air Quality Assessment Rev A, Air Quality Neutral Assessment, Construction Dust Assessment). All works which form part of the scheme, including any remedial measures, shall be completed before the development is first occupied and shall be retained in operation thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of Air Quality and safeguarding neighbouring amenities.

Condition : 35 - The Bird Hazard Management Plan hereby approved shall be implemented and shall remain in force for the life of the buildings. No subsequent alterations to the plan are to take place unless first submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: It is necessary to manage the flat roofs to minimise its attractiveness to birds which could endanger the safe movement of aircraft and the operation of Heathrow Airport.

Condition : 36 - All refuse and recycling bins and delivery carts in association with the approved development are to be stored within the building(s) at all times and only brought out when deliveries are being made or refuse collected.
Reason: To protect the quality of the local environment and to prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the development.

Condition : 37 - The approved details pertaining to fire safety and dignified means of escape shall be implemented within each unit prior to its occupation and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In the interest of safety of occupiers of the development.
